questions.q: What did David and Alan see when they reached the top of the brae above James's house?
choices: Soldiers camped all around the farm with fires
People hurrying about the house carrying lighted brands
A dark house with every window shut tight
The house burning after a night raid by the Campbell men
questions.evidence: five or six persons were moving hurriedly about, each carrying a lighted brand

questions.q: How did Alan let the people at the house know it was a friend coming?
choices: He fired his pistol into the air
He whistled three times in a special way
He called out his name in the Gaelic
He waved a burning torch to and fro from the hill-top
questions.evidence: he whistled three times, in a particular manner

questions.q: Why did Alan say it would be better to "give his name the go-by" when introducing David?
choices: So nobody could later tell the soldiers who David was
Because David's name was a Campbell name
Because David had asked to be called by a new name in Appin
So that James would not ask David for money
questions.evidence: it will be the better for his health if we give his name the go-by

questions.q: How did James of the Glens feel about the death of Colin Roy?
choices: He was glad and thanked Alan for the deed
He wished Colin were alive, fearing Appin would pay
He did not care and talked only of the farm
He was sure the soldiers would never suspect anyone in Appin
questions.evidence: I wish he was alive again

questions.q: James asks, "who's to bear the wyte of it?" What does "wyte" mean?
choices: Cost
Blame
Weight
Grief

questions.q: What were the servants taking out of the thatch of the house?
choices: Guns, swords and weapons of war
Bags of hidden gold and silver
Letters from Ardshiel in France
Bundles of tartan cloth and kilts
questions.evidence: from which they brought out guns, swords, and different weapons of war

questions.q: Why did Alan grab the bundle the lassie was carrying out of the house?
choices: It held the money he needed for the journey
It was his French clothes, which they meant to bury
It had papers that could hang James
It held food he wanted for the heather

questions.q: What was James's eldest son doing in the kitchen?
choices: Burning papers one by one
Cleaning his father's pistols
Packing food for Alan and David
Writing a letter to Edinburgh
questions.evidence: now and again setting one alight and burning it to the bitter end

questions.q: James shouts at his son, "Are you gone gyte?" What does "gyte" mean?
choices: Lazy
Deaf
Mad
Blind

questions.q: What new shoes was David given at James's house?
choices: Highland brogues of deer-leather
Heavy boots with iron nails
Soldier's shoes
Soft slippers made of sheep's wool from Mull
questions.evidence: a pair of Highland brogues made of deer-leather

questions.q: Which of these did James give Alan and David to take into the heather?
choices: A horse, a tent and a map
A bag of oatmeal, an iron pan and French brandy
A fishing net, a lantern and a blanket
Bread, cheese, a warm plaid and a small purse of guineas
questions.evidence: a bag of oatmeal, an iron pan, and a bottle of right French brandy

questions.q: Why did the three of them have so little money among them?
choices: Soldiers had searched the house and taken it
Alan's belt was gone and James had spent his on the tenants' law cases
David had lost his purse in the wood of Lettermore
They had buried all of it with the guns and swords
questions.evidence: legal expenses on behalf of the tenants

questions.q: What did James say he would have to do against Alan and David to protect himself?
choices: Lock them in the barn for the soldiers
Put out a paper offering a reward for them
Tell the soldiers exactly which way they had gone over the hill
Send them to the Campbells at Inverara
questions.evidence: have to offer a reward for ye

questions.q: Why did Alan grow angry when James wanted to describe David's clothes in the paper?
choices: Because David had just been given those clothes
Because the clothes were Alan's own
Because nobody had seen David's clothes
Because James had the colour of the coat all wrong
questions.evidence: Would ye change his clothes and then betray him?

questions.q: When David says to paper the man who really fired the shot, what can he tell from how Alan and James react?
choices: That the shooter was probably a Cameron from Mamore
That Alan himself was the man who fired the shot
That James had paid a stranger to kill Glenure
That the shooter was one of the Campbell servants
questions.evidence: it must have been a Cameron from Mamore that did the act

questions.q: What did Mrs. Stewart do right after David agreed to be papered?
choices: She scolded James for asking such a thing
She wept on their necks and blessed them
She ran out to warn the servants
She gave David her husband's sword
questions.evidence: wept first upon my neck and then on Alan's

questions.q: Alan says there will be "crying of 'Cruachan!'" the next day. What is "Cruachan"?
choices: A Stewart war song
The rallying-word of the Campbells
A nickname the people use for the King's dragoons
A Gaelic word for murder

questions.q: Why is this chapter called "The House of Fear"?
choices: The house is said to be haunted by ghosts
Everyone there is in a panic over what the murder will bring
Alan is afraid to go inside his kinsman's house
David is afraid James will hand him to the soldiers that night
questions.evidence: The faces in the torchlight were like those of people overborne with hurry and panic
